title: The Gold the Guards Laughed At

beats.voiceover: In 1923, a treasure hunter left the jungle with a bag of gold. Forty armed guards watched him go. They were laughing.
beats.visual: A lone treasure hunter walks out of thick jungle with a heavy bag while armed guards laugh behind him.

beats.voiceover: He did not fight them. He did not pay them. They had planned to kill him.
beats.visual: Forty armed guards stand in a half circle around the treasure hunter, hands resting on their rifles.

beats.voiceover: In an old temple, they found gold bars. The hunter held up a bar and cut it. Under the yellow, it was grey. "Fake," he cried. Then he hid a small clay pot under his coat.
beats.visual: Inside a torch-lit stone temple, the hunter cuts a yellow bar with a knife and slips a clay pot under his coat.

beats.voiceover: The leader saw the pot and took it. Something moved inside. One guard reached for another bar. "Leave it," said the leader. "It is worth nothing." They left with the pot.
beats.visual: The guard leader shakes a small clay pot beside his ear while another guard reaches toward a pile of yellow bars.

beats.voiceover: Only that one bar was fake. He had brought it from home. That night, the guards broke the pot. Inside were small stones.
beats.visual: At night by a campfire, angry guards stare at a broken clay pot and a small pile of grey stones.

title: The Duel He Won Sitting Still

beats.voiceover: In 1604, a blind old sword maker beat the best samurai in Japan. Three thousand people watched. The old man never touched his sword.
beats.visual: A thin blind old man faces a tall armored samurai in a dusty arena filled with a huge crowd.

beats.voiceover: He did not use poison. Nobody helped him. He only sat down.
beats.visual: The old man stands calm with empty hands, his sword still at his side, as the crowd watches in silence.

beats.voiceover: The samurai wanted a fight to the death. The old man asked for one thing. "I cannot see. Draw a circle around us. The man who leaves it loses." The samurai laughed and agreed.
beats.visual: A servant draws a wide circle in the dust around the blind old man and the smiling samurai.

beats.voiceover: Then the old man sat down. The samurai lifted his sword. The crowd shouted, "Shame!" No samurai can kill a blind man who only sits. He lowered his sword.
beats.visual: The old man sits on the ground inside the circle while the samurai holds his sword high above him.

beats.voiceover: For an hour he stood there while people laughed. At last, red with anger, he walked out of the circle. The old man smiled. He had never learned to fight.
beats.visual: The red-faced samurai steps over the line in the dust as the seated old man smiles and the crowd laughs.

title: The Thief Who Called the Police

beats.voiceover: In 1978, one thief took four million dollars from a money truck in Chicago. Twenty police officers carried the bags for him.
beats.visual: Police officers carry heavy cash bags from a money truck toward a plain white van on a city street.

beats.voiceover: He had no gun. He had no partner. He did not even hide his face.
beats.visual: A calm man with empty hands and an uncovered face stands beside a money truck in daylight.

beats.voiceover: In an orange work vest, he stopped the truck outside the bank. "Gas under the street," he shouted. "Everybody out!" The guards would not leave the money.
beats.visual: A man in an orange work vest raises one hand to stop a money truck outside a bank.

beats.voiceover: He smiled. "Good. Do not trust me. Call the police." They did, and twenty officers came. He pointed at his van. "The money is not safe here. Move it there." The officers wanted to be heroes.
beats.visual: The man in the orange vest points at a white van while police officers gather around the money truck.

beats.voiceover: They carried every bag to his van. He drove to the end of the street. Then he kept driving. The police guarded the empty truck for an hour.
beats.visual: A white van turns the corner at the end of the street while officers stand guard around an empty truck.

topic: Arctic ship crew that turns on its captain
title: The Captain's One Sentence

beats.voiceover: In 1897, a crew threw their captain off the ship, onto the ice. They kept all the food. Three nights later, they begged him to return.
beats.visual: Sailors push their captain down a rope ladder onto white sea ice beside a wooden ship frozen in place.

beats.voiceover: He did not fight them. He did not steal the food. He did not tell one lie.
beats.visual: The captain stands alone on the ice with empty hands, looking up at the crew on the deck.

beats.voiceover: Before he left, he asked for one small thing. He wanted to count the food. The crew laughed. He counted slowly. Then he said one sentence and walked onto the ice.
beats.visual: In the ship's food room, the captain counts wooden boxes one by one while sailors laugh behind him.

beats.voiceover: "Do not listen!" the leader shouted. Too late. That night, nobody slept. Every man watched the food. Every man watched the others.
beats.visual: At night below deck, tired sailors sit awake around a locked food room door, watching each other by lantern light.

beats.voiceover: His sentence was true. "There is enough food until spring, if nobody takes extra." On the third night, they gave him the key to the food. He kept it until spring.
beats.visual: The crew leader holds out a single iron key to the captain as he climbs back onto the ship.

topic: Wild West card game for a gold mine
title: The Letter on the Card Table

beats.voiceover: In 1882, a stranger won a gold mine in one card game. He had the worst cards at the table. He never looked at them.
beats.visual: A quiet stranger sits at a card table in a crowded saloon with two cards lying face down before him.

beats.voiceover: He did not cheat. Nobody helped him. The rich man held four kings.
beats.visual: A rich man in a fine suit smiles as he holds four kings close to his chest.

beats.voiceover: The rich man had stolen that mine from the stranger's father. The stranger bet all his money. Then he put a closed letter on the table. "If I lose, the judge opens this tonight."
beats.visual: The stranger pushes a pile of money forward and lays a closed letter on the card table.

beats.voiceover: The rich man laughed. "Open it now." The stranger pushed it closer. "You open it. Read it to everyone." The room went quiet. The rich man's hand did not move.
beats.visual: The stranger slides the closed letter toward the rich man, whose hand stops above it while the crowd watches.

beats.voiceover: He threw down his four kings. "Take the mine," he said, and left town that night. The stranger burned the letter. It was an empty page.
beats.visual: The stranger holds a burning sheet of paper over a candle while the rich man's chair sits empty behind him.

beats.voiceover: In 1214, a poor shepherd visited three kings. Each king gave him all his gold. And each king was happy about it.
beats.visual: A shepherd in old clothes walks into a stone castle hall where a smiling king sits beside chests of gold.

beats.voiceover: He did not fight. He did not steal. He carried only a stick and a bag.
beats.visual: The shepherd stands alone in the castle hall with a wooden stick and a heavy bag over his shoulder.

beats.voiceover: He pulled out a piece of black dragon skin, as big as a shield. "A dragon sleeps between your three lands," he said. Then he began to cry. "I cannot kill it. I can only lead it away."
beats.visual: The shepherd kneels and holds up a huge black piece of hard skin while the king leans forward to look.

beats.voiceover: Each king laughed. Then each king had the same dark idea. Pay the shepherd, and the dragon goes to my enemies. In secret, each one paid him everything.
beats.visual: Behind closed doors in three different castles, three kings hand the shepherd heavy bags of gold.

beats.voiceover: There was no dragon. The skin was iron, painted black. The shepherd went home rich. And three kings waited for their enemies' towns to burn.
beats.visual: The shepherd rides a cart full of gold down a mountain road while three distant castles watch the sky for smoke.

topic: 1700s pirates and a greedy port mayor
title: The Paper That Trapped the Mayor

beats.voiceover: In 1721, forty pirates were going to hang at sunrise. At midnight, the mayor opened their cells himself. By sunrise, the mayor was the one waiting to hang.
beats.visual: A tall gallows stands in a harbor square before sunrise while forty pirates in chains wait in dark cells.

beats.voiceover: The captain did not break out. He did not pay anyone. The king's officer was coming at sunrise.
beats.visual: A pirate captain sits alone in a dark cell and watches the last candle burn low.

beats.voiceover: The captain cried and begged the mayor. "I hid a treasure on an island. Free us, and it is yours. Just sign a paper for the port guards."
beats.visual: The pirate captain kneels and cries in front of the mayor, who holds a pen over a paper.

beats.voiceover: The greedy mayor wanted that gold. He would say the pirates broke out. At midnight, he signed and opened the cells. A guard saw him, but said nothing.
beats.visual: At midnight, the mayor unlocks a row of cells while a young guard watches from the shadows.

beats.voiceover: There was no treasure. The captain left the signed paper at the port. The king's officer read it at sunrise. The rope was ready. Only the man had changed.
beats.visual: At sunrise, the king's officer reads a paper at the port and points at the pale mayor beside the gallows.

topic: 1889 Texas, one man against twelve bank robbers
title: Twelve Robbers Broke Into Jail

beats.voiceover: In 1889, one man caught twelve bank robbers in one night. He never fired his gun. They broke into the jail themselves.
beats.visual: A small Texas jail stands dark and quiet at night while twelve riders stop their horses outside.

beats.voiceover: He did not chase them. He did not fight them. He only asked to join them.
beats.visual: A lone man with empty hands walks toward a campfire where twelve rough men sit with guns.

beats.voiceover: He walked into their camp with his hands up. "Let me join you," he said. "Tonight, the bank is hiding its gold in the town jail. It is in the first cell."
beats.visual: The man stands by the campfire with his hands up as the gang leader studies him closely.

beats.voiceover: At midnight, they broke in. The gold was there. The leader did not trust the new man near it. "You stay outside and watch the door." All twelve robbers ran into the cell.
beats.visual: Inside the jail, gold bars shine in an open cell as robbers rush in and one man waits by the door.

beats.voiceover: The new man closed the cell door and turned the key. Twelve robbers shouted behind the bars. The gold was real. So was the lock.
beats.visual: The man by the door turns a key in the cell lock as twelve robbers grab the bars from inside.
